clue.text: Flower festival not starting

indicators.note: a festival not starting loses its opening letter

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

explanation.surface: A flower show is billed as a festival that never quite gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden plant, so it is one example of a flower.

clue.text: 23 in every respect

definitions.meaning: the answer to 23 down, meaning unclothed; an idiom for naked

explanation.walkthrough: '23' points to the answer at 23 down, NUDE; being 'in the altogether' is a jokey idiom for being naked.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a state of nakedness (idiom), and the adverb means totally or wholly.

clue.text: Tropical tree supplying river in Devon's source

parts.note: the Tamar is the river forming the border of Devon and Cornwall
taken as written

indicators.note: a word's source is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tree is said to be fed by a river rising in the English county of Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is a river in south-west England dividing Devon from Cornwall, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a leguminous tree of tropical regions, grown for its sour pods.

clue.text: Triangle to be redrawn with reference

indicators.note: a figure to be redrawn is sketched afresh, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A geometry instruction: redraw the triangle, with reference to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to and with reference to are interchangeable phrases meaning concerning or about.

clue.text: I miss putting egg on first — it's wasteful

indicators.note: the prodding piece is placed at the front, before the rest

parts.note: to egg on is to urge or prod
a miss is a girl, or gal

explanation.surface: A cook regrets cracking an egg on first, as it proved a waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... first' moves PROD to the front of I + GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means recklessly extravagant, spending freely: a synonym for wasteful.

clue.text: Top-class post office shut up

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A smart post office that has closed its doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh is informal British for upper-class, smart or luxurious.

clue.text: Potter in bundle, upset and led astray

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word over, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: a wad is a bundle, e.g. of notes

indicators.note: led astray means these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A potter, upset over a bundle, has been led astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a ceramicist; it is the verb meaning to amble about.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to move about idly, a synonym for dawdle or loiter.

clue.text: Ruby, perhaps, and I following popular heavenly duo

indicators.note: the letter I comes after the word for popular

parts.note: a ruby is an example of a gem
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A girl named Ruby and I follow a celebrated pair of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins Castor and Pollux, is the constellation of two bright stars.

clue.text: Three students welcoming university break

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: L (learner) is the crossword student, so three of them are LLL

explanation.surface: Three students let a university in during their break.
explanation.definitionFit: A lull is a pause or quiet interval, a temporary break in activity.

clue.text: Enduring not having a date?

definitions.meaning: lasting for ever, never going out of fashion
read as without any time or date fixed to it

explanation.walkthrough: 'not having a date' tempts toward romance; it means lacking a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting is unaffected by passing years, and read literally it lacks a fixed time.

clue.text: Give William printed sheet

parts.note: to hand is to give
Bill is a short form of William

explanation.surface: Pass a printed leaflet to someone called William.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbill is a small printed notice or leaflet handed out to people.

clue.text: Row right after broadcast — it gets many people up in the air

definitions.text: it gets many people up in the air

indicators.note: the row and right pieces come behind the broadcast piece

parts.note: to air is to broadcast
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A broadcast row is followed by a jet that infuriates many people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in the air' suggests annoyance or uncertainty; here it means literally aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger jet carries many travellers through the sky, a playful description.

clue.text: Rubbish in entrance, it's enough to take one's breath away

definitions.text: it's enough to take one's breath away

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Junk in a doorway, something breathtaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take one's breath away' sounds like awe; here it is grimly literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A garotte is a cord or wire used for strangling, literally stopping the victim's breathing.

clue.text: Strange doodle artist's framed in fabulous place

indicators.note: the artist piece sits inside, as a picture in a frame
something strange is odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: An artist's odd doodle is framed in some wonderful place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' is the anagram signal and 'framed in' the container; RA (Royal Academician) is the stock crossword artist, with the 's only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado is the legendary city of gold, a mythical land of riches.

clue.text: Thief left with fire-raiser, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is as heard, not as written

parts.note: L for left, plus arsonist, someone who sets fires

explanation.surface: A thief has been left with an arsonist, so the reports say.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the crime of theft, so one who commits it is a thief.

clue.text: Match steps required in trial for 10?

parts.note: a test is a cricket match, a Test match
a flight is a set of stairs or steps

explanation.surface: Practice steps are needed before a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers to the answer at 10 down, AIRLINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane on trial takes a trial run in the sky before going into service.

clue.text: Cook maybe prospered thus and enjoyed a long life

definitions.meaning: Alastair Cook, the England cricketer, would succeed by batting a long time
an idiom for having lived to old age

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' is Alastair Cook, a former England cricket captain; an innings is a batsman's turn at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a long, productive turn at batting, and by idiom a full lifespan.

clue.text: TV programme from novel's supported by actors

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the other piece is below

parts.note: novel means new, plus the 's
the actors in a production are its cast

explanation.surface: A television drama adapted from a novel, carried by its actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A newscast is a broadcast bulletin of news, a kind of television show.

clue.text: Hooter goes before dodgy club go into decline

indicators.note: one piece goes ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: hooter is slang for nose
a dive is a disreputable bar or nightclub

explanation.surface: A siren sounds before a seedy club starts to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: To nosedive is to fall steeply, as a plane does, so to decline sharply.

clue.text: Share beer and philosophy

parts.note: a ration is a share or allowance
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Splitting a pint and talking philosophy, a pub scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or principles behind something.

clue.text: Note curdled milk on the turn

indicators.note: on the turn means turning round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: rennet can mean curdled milk from a calf's stomach, used in cheesemaking

explanation.surface: A memo warns that the milk has curdled and is going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the turn' is said of milk going sour; here it signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound banknote.

clue.text: Choose not to take part in work with solicitor

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a tout is someone soliciting custom

explanation.surface: Declining to join in a job alongside one's lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer; it means one who solicits.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw or decline to participate is a direct synonym phrase.

clue.text: Square fellow

definitions.meaning: ... Square is a garden square in Bloomsbury, London
a man's name, e.g. ... Crowe or the philosopher Bertrand ...

explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'square fellow' means a dull man; Russell Square is a well-known London square.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a London square and is also a common male first name.

clue.text: Backing bridge partners when one's in action

parts.note: South, S, partners North at bridge

indicators.note: one partner is placed inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
North, N, is the other half of the bridge partnership

explanation.surface: Supporting one's bridge partners when one is in play.
explanation.walkthrough: North and South form a bridge partnership: S goes first and N goes in ACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanction can mean official approval or support, synonymous with backing.

clue.text: Call for similar cards

parts.note: in the children's card game, players shout this word when two matching cards turn up

explanation.definitionFit: In the game, the word shouted when two identical cards appear wins the pile.

clue.text: One discovered coming from dune?

indicators.note: coming from implies being rearranged out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone found on a sand dune, such as a naturist on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uncovered is not covered by clothes, i.e. naked.

clue.text: Greek character returned racing around without concern

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek figure comes back from motor racing, unconcerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the Greek letter round, and 'around' looks like a container signal but here scrambles the racing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Callous or indifferent, lacking care or sympathy, is to be without concern.

clue.text: Incomplete sentence? Labour can be limited this way

definitions.text: Labour can be limited this way

parts.note: partial, so part
a prison sentence is time, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A grammar comment about an unfinished sentence, followed by a remark on limiting work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the UK political party; it is work.
explanation.definitionFit: Working fewer hours than the full week restricts the amount of work done.

clue.text: Sound of bird, small, in dry surroundings

indicators.note: the small piece goes inside
the dry piece forms the surroundings around the other

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol, i.e. dry
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A little bird chirps in an arid landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is the short high chirp made by a small songbird.
